rules.statement: When a session-start hook runs several setup scripts that make network calls (git clone, tool downloads), bound each script with its own timeout (for example GNU `timeout`, which signals the whole process group), report a timeout as a one-line message and continue with the next script.
rules.why: With no timeout, a stalled download in one script can use up the shared hook time limit, so the later scripts never run and the session is left without the tools they install.
rules.check: Look for hook or setup scripts whose network commands, or the scripts themselves, run without a timeout ahead of other required setup steps. Check that the per-script limits together fit within the hook's overall timeout.

rules.statement: In PowerShell test scripts, don't ask for a failure detail built with member enumeration (such as `$entries.command`) to be narrowed to the first element (`$entries[0].command`) when the check also rejects having more than one entry.
rules.why: Member enumeration is never empty when there is an entry, and it shows every entry's value, so the failure message exposes the extra entries the check rejects. `[0]` would hide them.
rules.check: Before reporting a mismatch between the checked expression and the failure detail, see whether the check covers a multiple-entry case that the enumerated detail is meant to show.

rules.statement: Reflow comment-based help paragraphs (such as `.DESCRIPTION`) so every line fills evenly up to the 120-character limit, with no line much shorter than the rest and none over 120 characters.
rules.why: Help text with a short line left after an edit reads unevenly, and lines over the limit break the line-length convention.
rules.check: Look in edited help or doc-comment paragraphs for a line that breaks mid-phrase well short of the width, and for any line longer than 120 characters.
